correctness.rationale: For odd n=2k+3>=3, m=(2^n+1)/3, the pole semigroup <4,m> gives differential basis x^i y^j dx with j=0,1,2, 4i+jm<=3m-5. Reading RESULT.md and the actual Cartier verifier establishes transition rules (j=0 odd -> ((i-1)/2,0), j=1 odd -> ((i-1)/2,2), j=1 even -> ((i+m-1)/2,0), j=2 odd -> ((i-1)/2,1), others zero). For C^(n-1), the j=1 alternating route followed by exit to j=0 requires s≡I_{k-r} mod 4^(k-r+1) in a bounded range, uniquely yielding initial indices indexed r=0..k and terminal exponents (2*4^r-2)/3. Initial j=0 and j=2 paths fail the necessary index bounds. Terminal exponents are even, hence C^n=0, while rank(C^(n-1))=k+1=(n-1)/2>0. Semilinear nonzero images over an algebraically closed perfect field have these dimensions. Independently implemented basis transition and enumerated n=3,5,7,9,11,13,15,17 (basis sizes 3,15,63,255,1023,4095,16383,65535): all exact terminal images/ranks and subsequent vanishing checked. Finite checks corroborate only; infinite proof is the congruence and exclusion argument.
